name: Greater Somalia

furtherReading.title: Greater Somalia (Wikipedia)
furtherReading.note: Overview of the territories, history and wars behind the idea.

furtherReading.title: Somalia: Pan-Somalism (Library of Congress Country Study)
furtherReading.note: Explains the five-pointed star, the border treaties dispute and the Kenyan NFD.

furtherReading.title: Somali Constitution of 1960 (English)
furtherReading.note: The founding text, including the article on promoting union of Somali territories.

scope: The mainstream pan-Somali nationalism of the independence era (Somali Youth League, the 1960 Somali Republic constitution, the five-pointed star flag, the 1960s claims on Ogaden and the NFD), with its post-1969 and Barre-era armed form noted but not treated as the core. It excludes Barre's scientific socialism as such, the Islamist (al-Shabaab) appropriation of the idea, and Somaliland or Puntland separatism.

summary: Greater Somalia (pan-Somalism) holds that the Somali people, divided by European and Ethiopian partition among Somalia, Djibouti, Ethiopia's Ogaden and Kenya's Northern Frontier District, should be united in one state, on the ground of self-determination and the invalidity of the colonial-era treaties. Its independence-era form pursued this officially by legal and peaceful means while a radical wing wanted any means and the state built a large army. It has no distinctive economic doctrine.
